posture_tips: Hang from the bar with an overhand grip slightly wider than your shoulders and your arms fully extended.
Keep your chest up, legs together and core braced so you don't swing.
Pull your shoulder blades down first, then pull until your chin clears the bar; lower under control to a full hang.
Don't kip with your legs or cut reps short with your elbows still bent at the bottom.
Lower yourself off the bar under control at the end of the set instead of dropping from the top.
Grip the bar overhand about 1.5x shoulder width and hang with your arms straight.
Drive your chest toward the bar and keep your elbows pointing out and down.
Pull your elbows toward your ribs until your upper chest nears the bar, then lower over 2-3 seconds.
Don't go so wide that you lose range of motion or your shoulders shrug up toward your ears.
Pick a grip width that lets you complete the full range without shoulder discomfort.
Hang from the parallel handles with your palms facing each other and your arms fully extended.
Keep your ribs down and lean your torso back slightly as you pull up.
Pull with your elbows tight to your body until your chin clears the handles, then lower without rushing.
Don't shrug at the start; depress your shoulder blades before you bend your elbows.
If you add weight, secure the belt or dumbbell so it doesn't swing between your legs.
Grip the bar shoulder-width with palms facing you and hang with your arms straight.
Keep your torso steady and your elbows in front of your body, pointing at the floor.
Pull until your chin is over the bar, squeezing your lats, then lower all the way to a full hang.
Don't stop halfway on the way down; reaching full extension trains the lats in their stretched position.
Add load gradually and keep every rep technically clean.
Set the counterweight, place your knees or feet on the platform and grab the top handles.
Keep your torso upright and your chest up without leaning onto the platform.
Pull until your chin passes the handles, then lower slowly until your arms are fully straight.
Don't use so much assistance that the platform launches you; reduce it as you get stronger.
Keep both hands on the handles as you step on and off so the platform doesn't jolt.
Loop the band over the bar and place a knee or foot in it before hanging with an overhand grip.
Keep your body in a straight line and your core tight so the band doesn't swing you.
Pull until your chin is over the bar and lower under control, without letting the band snap you up.
Don't rely on a thick band forever; switch to a lighter one once you hit your target reps.
Check the band for nicks and make sure it's securely looped before every set.

name_es: Jalón al pecho en polea (agarre ancho)
posture_tips: Set the thigh pad snug over your legs and grip the bar overhand, wider than your shoulders.
Lean back a few degrees with your chest up and your lower back neutral.
Pull the bar to your upper chest by driving your elbows down, then let it rise until your lats stretch.
Don't pull the bar behind your neck or rock your torso back to move more weight.
Return the bar to the top before standing up so the plates don't slam.

name_es: Jalón al pecho en polea (agarre neutro)
posture_tips: Attach a neutral-grip handle, sit with your thighs under the pad and your arms fully extended.
Keep your chest up and your elbows close to your body, pointing at the floor.
Pull the handle to your sternum by driving your elbows to your sides, then return slowly to full extension.
Don't round your back at the end of the pull to bring the handle closer to your chest.
Make sure the carabiner on the handle is fully closed before loading the stack.

name_es: Jalón al pecho en polea (a una mano)
posture_tips: Sit under the high pulley with a single handle and your working arm fully stretched overhead.
Keep your torso square and stable, without twisting toward the working side.
Drive your elbow down toward your hip on a slight diagonal, then let the arm rise to stretch the lat.
Don't compensate by leaning sideways; the movement should come from the shoulder and elbow.
Start with your weaker arm and match the reps on the other side.

name_es: Jalón al pecho en polea (agarre supino)
posture_tips: Grip a straight bar shoulder-width with palms facing you and lock your thighs under the pad.
Keep your chest up with a slight lean back, without over-arching your lower back.
Pull the bar to your lower chest with elbows tucked to your sides, then return under control.
Don't turn it into a biceps curl: think about driving the elbows down, not bending the wrists.
Use a weight you can control on the way up without it lifting you off the seat.
Adjust the seat so you can reach the handles with arms extended and palms facing you.
Brace firmly against the chest or thigh pad and keep your back neutral.
Pull the handles down and back along the machine's arc, then return slowly to a full stretch.
Don't lift off the seat or pad to gain range with momentum.
Check that the weight pin is fully inserted before you start.

name_es: Jalón al pecho en máquina de discos
posture_tips: Load the plates evenly on both sides, lock your thighs under the pad and grab the handles.
Keep your chest up and your torso still throughout the movement.
Pull the handles to the sides of your chest, then let them rise slowly until your arms are straight.
Don't let the handles fly up at the top; control the eccentric on every rep.
Load and unload plates with the machine at rest, alternating sides so it doesn't tip out of balance.
Grip the bar overhand slightly wider than shoulders, knees soft, and hinge your torso to about 45 degrees.
Keep your back neutral and neck in line, eyes on the floor slightly ahead of you.
Row the bar to your navel while squeezing your shoulder blades, then lower to straight arms without moving.
Don't stand up on each rep to heave the bar up with momentum.
If you can't hold a neutral back, drop the load before continuing.
Grip the bar shoulder-width with palms facing forward and hinge at the hips.
Keep your torso angled and locked, core braced and the bar close to your thighs.
Row the bar to your lower abs, driving your elbows back and close to your body.
Don't flex your wrists or turn the row into a biceps curl.
Lift the bar off the floor with a neutral back and your legs, never with a rounded back.
Set up with the bar on the floor over midfoot and your torso nearly parallel to the ground.
Keep your back flat and hips high, holding the same torso angle from rep to rep.
Row the bar explosively to your stomach and return it to the floor each rep, coming to a dead stop.
Don't lift your torso to help the bar up; if you need to, the load is too heavy.
Set the bar down under control rather than dropping it, to protect your back and the equipment.
Set the safeties at knee height, grip the bar overhand and hinge your torso from the hips.
Position yourself so the bar travels straight to your stomach without hitting your thighs.
Row the bar to your navel squeezing your shoulder blades, then lower under control to straight arms.
Don't stand too close or too far from the bar; the fixed path demands precise positioning.
Rotate the bar to re-rack it on the hooks before letting go at the end.
Lie face down on a high flat bench with the bar beneath you and your arms hanging straight.
Keep your chest and hips on the bench and your head in line with your torso.
Row the bar until it touches the underside of the bench, then lower slowly to full extension.
Don't lift your chest off the bench to gain range; you lose support and tension.
Make sure the bench is stable on boxes or supports before you lie on it.
Straddle the anchored bar with a V-handle under the plates and your knees bent.
Keep your torso at about 45 degrees and your back neutral throughout the pull.
Row the handle to your lower chest driving your elbows back, then lower until your arms are straight.
Don't load big plates that shorten your range or force you to swing.
Secure the end of the bar in a landmine or corner so it can't slide.

name_es: Remo en T en máquina de discos (con apoyo de pecho)
posture_tips: Step onto the platform, rest your chest on the pad and grab the handles with straight arms.
Keep your chest on the pad and your neck neutral without lifting your head.
Row the handles toward your torso squeezing your shoulder blades, then lower the load under control.
Don't peel your chest off the pad to push with your legs at the end of the pull.
Step on and off the platform only with the load in its resting position.
Stand perpendicular to the anchored bar, grip the end overhand and rest your free forearm on your knee.
Keep your hips high, torso hinged and back neutral without rotating.
Row the end of the bar toward your hip with the elbow flared, then lower until your lat stretches.
Don't twist your torso open to move the load; keep rotation minimal.
Use smaller plates for more range of motion and anchor the bar securely before you start.
Place one knee and one hand on the bench, with the dumbbell hanging under the shoulder of your free arm.
Keep your back flat and parallel to the floor, with your shoulders level.
Pull the dumbbell toward your hip brushing your side, then lower until your lat stretches.
Don't rotate your torso up on each rep to lift more weight.
Pick up and put down the dumbbell with a neutral back while supported on the bench.
Hold a dumbbell in each hand, soften your knees and hinge your torso from the hips.
Keep your back neutral and your weight spread across your whole foot.
Row both dumbbells toward your waist with elbows close to your body, then lower them slowly.
Don't let your head drop or your shoulders round forward on the way down.
If your lower back tires before your upper back, switch to the chest-supported version.

name_es: Remo con mancuernas con apoyo de pecho
posture_tips: Lie face down on a bench inclined to about 30-45 degrees with a dumbbell in each hand.
Keep your chest on the pad and your toes planted on the floor so you don't slide.
Row by driving your elbows back until your shoulder blades squeeze, then lower to straight arms.
Don't crane your neck to look forward; keep your gaze toward the floor.
Set the dumbbells on the floor before getting up from the bench.
Take a staggered stance, brace your free hand on a bench or thigh and grip the kettlebell handle.
Keep your torso hinged and stable, with your hips square to the floor.
Row the kettlebell toward your hip keeping your wrist straight, then lower under control.
Don't let the kettlebell swing between reps; come to a stop at the bottom of each one.
Grip the handle firmly and make sure you have clear space around you as you row.
Sit with your feet on the platform, knees slightly bent, holding the V-handle with arms extended.
Keep your torso upright and still, chest up and shoulders away from your ears.
Row the handle to your stomach squeezing your shoulder blades, then extend letting your shoulders reach forward.
Don't rock your torso back and forth to move the weight with your lower back.
Grab and release the handle with your knees bent so you don't yank on your lower back.
Attach a long bar, grip it overhand wider than your shoulders and sit with your back upright.
Keep your elbows flared about 60-70 degrees from your torso and your chest up.
Row the bar to your lower chest squeezing your mid-back, then return slowly.
Don't shrug at the end of the pull; finish with your shoulder blades, not your neck.
Choose a weight you can control on the return without it pulling you forward.
Grip a straight bar shoulder-width with palms up and sit tall.
Keep your elbows tight to your body and your torso locked during the pull.
Row the bar to your navel driving your elbows back, then let it return until your arms are straight.
Don't lift or flare your elbows; you'd lose the emphasis on the lats.
Keep your wrists straight and in line with your forearms throughout the set.

name_es: Remo sentado en polea (a una mano)
posture_tips: Sit facing the pulley with a single handle and your arm extended forward.
Keep your shoulders level and torso stable, allowing only a slight rotation.
Row the handle toward your hip driving the elbow back, then extend letting your shoulder reach forward.
Don't twist your whole torso to finish the rep; the work should come from your back.
Start with your weaker side and brace your free hand on your thigh for stability.

name_es: Jalón en polea al pecho (agarre ancho)
posture_tips: Face the pulley with a long bar at chest height and take a wide overhand grip.
Keep your torso upright and chest up, elbows at or slightly below shoulder height.
Pull the bar to your chest flaring your elbows and squeezing your shoulder blades; return to straight arms.
Don't lean back to bring the bar closer; your torso shouldn't move.
Set the pulley height and weight before starting so you can pull without neck tension.

name_es: Remo con apoyo de pecho en máquina (agarre ancho)
posture_tips: Adjust the seat and pad so the wide handles sit at chest height with your arms extended.
Keep your chest on the pad and your elbows flared out to the sides.
Row back until your elbows pass your torso, squeeze your shoulder blades and return under control.
Don't pull your chest off the pad at the end of each rep to gain range.
Check the pin and seat height before every set.

name_es: Remo con apoyo de pecho en máquina (agarre neutro)
posture_tips: Sit with your chest against the pad and grab the vertical handles with palms facing each other.
Keep your back neutral and your elbows close to your body throughout the row.
Pull until your elbows are behind your torso, then straighten your arms without losing tension.
Don't shrug your shoulders or jut your head forward at the end of the pull.
Let the weight return to rest under control when you finish the set.

name_es: Remo con apoyo de pecho en máquina (agarre supino, a una mano)
posture_tips: Rest your chest on the pad and grab one handle palm up with your arm extended.
Keep your chest fixed and your shoulders square to the pad, without twisting your torso.
Drive your elbow back along your side toward your hip, then return slowly until your lat stretches.
Don't push against the machine with your free hand to assist the pull.
Train both sides with the same load and reps to keep things balanced.

name_es: Remo bajo en máquina de discos
posture_tips: Set the seat so your chest is against the pad and grab the low handles with your arms extended.
Keep your chest on the pad and your torso upright without leaning back.
Row the handles toward your hips driving your elbows back, then return until your back stretches.
Don't shorten the range; let your shoulder blades spread apart on every stretch.
Load plates evenly and strip them when you finish to leave the machine safe.

name_es: Remo alto en máquina de discos
posture_tips: Lock your thighs under the pad and grab the high handles with your arms extended overhead.
Keep your chest up with a slight forward lean, without arching your lower back.
Pull the handles down and back to the sides of your chest, then return under control to the top.
Don't let the weight lift you off the seat on the way up.
Adjust the thigh pad so you're locked in before loading heavy plates.
Set up under a bar fixed at hip height, grip it overhand and extend your body with heels on the floor.
Keep your body rigid like a plank, with glutes and abs squeezed.
Pull until your chest touches the bar squeezing your shoulder blades, then lower to straight arms.
Don't let your hips sag or rise before your chest during the pull.
Make sure the rack or Smith machine bar is securely locked before hanging from it.
Lie on the bench holding one dumbbell with both hands over your chest, elbows slightly bent.
Keep your ribs down and your lower back stable, without arching as the weight lowers.
Arc the dumbbell behind your head until you feel a stretch, then bring it back over your chest.
Don't bend and straighten your elbows each rep; keep the elbow angle fixed.
Cup the dumbbell under the top plate with interlocked hands so it can't slip.
Lie on a flat bench with the EZ bar over your chest using a narrow overhand grip.
Keep your head down, feet planted and elbows slightly bent throughout the arc.
Lower the bar behind your head until you feel the stretch, then bring it back over your chest.
Don't go past the point you can control or arch your back to chase more range.
Use a moderate load; the bar passes over your face and you must be able to stop it at any point.
Set the seat so your shoulders line up with the machine's pivot and rest your elbows on the pads.
Keep your back against the pad and fasten the seat belt if the machine has one.
Drive your elbows down in an arc to your sides, then return slowly until your lats stretch.
Don't pull with your hands; press through the back of your upper arms.
Align the pivot carefully; poor alignment loads the shoulder instead of the lats.

name_es: Jalón con brazos rectos en polea
posture_tips: Face the high pulley with a straight bar or rope, arms extended and torso leaning slightly forward.
Keep your elbows nearly locked and your back neutral, hips pushed slightly back.
Sweep the bar down in an arc to your thighs squeezing your lats, then let it rise to eye level.
Don't bend your elbows and turn it into a triceps pushdown.
Step back after grabbing the bar so the load doesn't pull you forward at the start.

name_es: Jalón con brazos rectos con banda
posture_tips: Anchor the band overhead, grab it with both hands and step back until there's tension.
Keep your arms straight, chest up and a slight hip hinge.
Sweep your hands down in an arc to your hips, then return slowly to shoulder height.
Don't shrug as the band pulls your arms back up.
Check the anchor and the band's condition; if it slips it can snap back at you.
Take the bar from a rack at thigh height with a shoulder-width overhand grip.
Keep your arms straight, chest up and chin neutral, without looking up.
Raise your shoulders straight up toward your ears, hold for a second and lower them fully.
Don't roll your shoulders in circles; the movement is straight up and down.
Unrack the bar from mid-thigh height instead of lifting it off the floor.
Stand with a dumbbell at each side and your palms facing your body.
Keep your arms relaxed and straight, neck long and eyes forward.
Shrug your shoulders as high as possible, pause briefly at the top and lower until your traps stretch.
Don't bend your elbows to help; your arms are just hooks.
Use straps if your grip gives out before your traps rather than dropping the dumbbells.
Step inside the hex bar, grab the high handles and lift it with your legs.
Keep your torso upright and your shoulders in line with the handles, without leaning.
Shrug your shoulders straight up, hold at the top and lower under control.
Don't roll your shoulders forward; think about lifting them vertically toward your ears.
Pick up and set down the bar with a neutral back, just like a deadlift.
Set the safeties at mid-thigh, grip the bar overhand and unrack it by rotating your wrists.
Keep your body close to the bar and your back straight throughout.
Raise your shoulders along the bar's path, squeeze at the top and lower through a full range.
Don't cut the range short with excessive loads; range matters more than weight.
Set the safety stops just below the starting position before you begin.
Attach a straight bar to the low pulley, grip it overhand and stand close to the stack.
Keep your arms straight and your torso vertical without leaning toward the pulley.
Shrug your shoulders toward your ears against the constant cable tension, then lower slowly.
Don't bounce at the bottom; use the cable's constant tension through the whole range.
Plant your feet firmly and stand close enough that the cable doesn't pull you off balance.
